# Problem codes

<!-- Generated by `budget problems --markdown` from problem_catalogue.py. -->

Every finding the tool reports has a **code**. This page says, for each code, what the rule is, why it matters and how to resolve it. The texts are the same for every project; they never contain a value from your files. A finding shows the file and the place in it; in the window and in the result files it also carries the value and the limit when the finding is a comparison (for example a mass over its limit). See [Read and fix problems](user-manual/read-and-fix-problems.md) for how to work through them and `budget problems CODE` for this text on the command line.

Severity is the usual one: **error** (the project cannot be used as it is, or a limit is broken), **warning** (results are produced, but something needs a look), **info** (nothing to fix). A finding that a result is *n/a* because of a placeholder is shown as *not checked* in the window.

## Reading the files

### YAML_SYNTAX

**The file is not valid YAML** (error)

- **Rule.** Every project file must be readable YAML within the tool's size and structure limits (no aliases that expand without bound, no oversized files).
- **Why it matters.** Nothing in a file that cannot be read is used; a result that needs it is missing.
- **What to do.** Fix the syntax at the line shown (indentation, colons, quotes). If the message names a size or alias limit, shorten the file or remove the aliases instead.

### FILE_NOT_FOUND

**A file or folder is missing** (error)

- **Rule.** The project folder, and every file that the project names, must exist and be readable.
- **Why it matters.** A missing file is a missing input; whatever needs it cannot be worked out.
- **What to do.** Check the path and the permissions. A project is a folder that holds project.yaml.

### FILE_INVALID

**The file cannot be used as a project file** (error)

- **Rule.** A project file must be a mapping of fields (name: value), and must lie inside the project folder (links that lead out are not followed).
- **Why it matters.** A file outside the folder would make the project depend on something the export does not contain.
- **What to do.** Write the file as fields, and keep it inside the project folder.

### KIND_MISMATCH

**The file has the wrong kind** (error)

- **Rule.** The location of a file decides its kind (a file in units/ is a unit); the `kind:` line must agree.
- **Why it matters.** A file read as the wrong kind would be checked against the wrong fields.
- **What to do.** Set `kind:` to the one the message names, or move the file to the right folder.

### ID_INVALID

**The id of a file is not valid** (error)

- **Rule.** The id (the file name without .yaml) must not be empty, must not start with a dot and must be valid text.
- **Why it matters.** Other files refer to a file by its id; an invalid id cannot be referred to reliably.
- **What to do.** Rename the file with letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

### ID_UNUSUAL

**The id of a file has unusual characters** (warning)

- **Rule.** An id should consist of ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `-`.
- **Why it matters.** Spaces, accents and look-alike letters make ids hard to type and to tell apart.
- **What to do.** Rename the file, and every reference to it, with letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

### ID_COLLISION

**Two ids differ only by capitals or accent encoding** (warning)

- **Rule.** Two ids in one folder must differ in more than capital letters or the way an accent is encoded.
- **Why it matters.** On some file systems (Windows among them) such names are one file, so the project would change meaning between computers.
- **What to do.** Rename one of the files.

### FILE_IGNORED

**A file is not used** (warning)

- **Rule.** Files that are not part of the project layout are not read.
- **Why it matters.** A value you wrote in an ignored file has no effect on any result.
- **What to do.** Move the file to the folder it belongs in, or delete it.

### FILE_MIGRATED

**The file was read from an older format** (info)

- **Rule.** A file with an older schema version is converted in memory when it is loaded.
- **Why it matters.** Nothing changes in your results; the file on disk is still the old version.
- **What to do.** Save the project to write the file in the current format.

### SCHEMA_VERSION_MISSING

**The file has no valid schema version** (error)

- **Rule.** Every file starts with `schema_version:`, a whole number from 1.
- **Why it matters.** The version tells the tool how to read the file.
- **What to do.** Add `schema_version:` with the number that the documentation names for the file kind.

### SCHEMA_TOO_NEW

**The file is from a newer version of the tool** (error)

- **Rule.** The schema version of a file must not be newer than the tool supports.
- **Why it matters.** A newer file may hold fields this version would silently misread.
- **What to do.** Open the project with a newer release of the tool.

### SCHEMA_MIGRATION_MISSING

**No migration exists for this old version** (error)

- **Rule.** Each old schema version needs a migration to the current one.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the file cannot be converted.
- **What to do.** Open the file with an older release of the tool, save it, and retry.

### SCHEMA_MIGRATION_FAILED

**The migration of the file failed** (error)

- **Rule.** A file of an old version must have the layout of that version to be converted.
- **Why it matters.** A file that does not match its stated version cannot be converted safely.
- **What to do.** Check `schema_version:` and the layout of the file against the documentation of that version.

## Fields and units

### FIELD_MISSING

**A required field is missing** (error)

- **Rule.** Each file kind has fields that must be present.
- **Why it matters.** A missing input would otherwise be silently replaced by a default; the tool never does that.
- **What to do.** Add the field. The hint names its unit when it has one.

### FIELD_UNKNOWN

**A field is not known** (error)

- **Rule.** Only the fields of the file kind are accepted.
- **Why it matters.** A misspelled field would be ignored and its default used, with no sign of it in the results.
- **What to do.** Correct the spelling (the hint suggests the nearest field) or remove the field.

### FIELD_INVALID

**A field has a value that cannot be used** (error)

- **Rule.** A value must have the type, range and unit of its field.
- **Why it matters.** A value outside what the model accepts would give a result that means nothing.
- **What to do.** Correct the value as the message says. A bare number is in the unit named in the field name (`power_w` is in watts); a value with a unit is converted.

### UNIT_INVALID

**A unit is not accepted** (error)

- **Rule.** A value with a unit must use a unit of the dimension of its field.
- **Why it matters.** A unit of another dimension, or an ambiguous one (the word `ton`), would change the number by a hidden factor.
- **What to do.** Write the unit the field expects, or a number in the field's unit.

### DUPLICATE_NAME

**A name is used twice** (error)

- **Rule.** Names that are looked up (power modes, buses, nodes, limits) must be unique in their list.
- **Why it matters.** A reference to a repeated name would be ambiguous.
- **What to do.** Rename one of the entries.

### DUPLICATE_ID

**An id is used twice** (error)

- **Rule.** Site ids must be unique across ground_stations/ and targets/.
- **Why it matters.** A scenario names a site by its id; two sites with one id cannot be told apart.
- **What to do.** Rename one of the files.

## Configuration

### SOURCE_MISSING

**A configuration number has no source** (error)

- **Rule.** Every configuration number carries a non-empty `source`.
- **Why it matters.** A number without a source cannot be reviewed; the tool never invents standards values.
- **What to do.** Cite the standard or data sheet, or write `TBD` to mark a placeholder.

### CONFIG_VALUE_INVALID

**A configuration number is out of range** (error)

- **Rule.** Each configuration number has a range in which it makes physical sense.
- **Why it matters.** A ratio above 1 or a negative temperature would produce results that look valid.
- **What to do.** Check the value and its unit. Ratios are fractions (0.1 means 10 %), temperatures are in kelvin, gains and losses in decibels.

### CONFIG_MISSING

**A configuration file is missing** (warning)

- **Rule.** A budget needs the configuration files it reads (margin policy, power configuration, mass limits, thermal files, tables).
- **Why it matters.** The results that need it are not computed (n/a); they are never filled with defaults.
- **What to do.** Create the file with every number sourced, or `TBD` for the ones you do not have yet.

### CONFIG_EMPTY_TABLE

**A configuration table has no entries** (warning)

- **Rule.** A table that a budget reads (mass limits, Eb/N0, attenuation) should have entries.
- **Why it matters.** With no entries the checks that use the table cannot run.
- **What to do.** Add entries from a cited source, or import them from a file.

### CONFIG_PLACEHOLDER

**A configuration number is a placeholder** (warning)

- **Rule.** A number whose source is `TBD`, or that has no value, is a placeholder.
- **Why it matters.** Every result that needs it is n/a; a result built on a guess would look like a pass.
- **What to do.** Replace it with a value from your margin policy, standard or data sheet and cite the source.

### RESULT_INCOMPLETE

**A result needs a placeholder** (warning)

- **Rule.** A result that depends on a placeholder or missing input is shown as n/a.
- **Why it matters.** It is neither a pass nor a fail; it has not been checked.
- **What to do.** Replace the placeholder named in the same report with a sourced value.

## References between files

### REF_UNKNOWN_BUS

**A unit names a supply bus that is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** The bus of a unit must be one of the buses listed in spacecraft.yaml.
- **Why it matters.** Power is summed by bus and each bus has its converter efficiency.
- **What to do.** Use the name of a bus listed under `buses`, or add the bus.

### REF_UNKNOWN_MATURITY

**A maturity class is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** The maturity class of a unit or expendable must be a class of the margin policy.
- **Why it matters.** The class decides the margin applied to its power and mass.
- **What to do.** Use a class listed under `classes` in config/margin_policy.yaml, or add the class.

### REF_UNKNOWN_UNIT

**A spacecraft mode names a unit that does not exist** (error)

- **Rule.** Every unit named in a spacecraft mode must be a file in units/.
- **Why it matters.** The mode's total would silently leave the unit out.
- **What to do.** Use the file name (without .yaml) of a unit.

### REF_UNKNOWN_UNIT_MODE

**A spacecraft mode names a power mode the unit does not have** (error)

- **Rule.** The power mode assigned to a unit must be one of the unit's own power modes.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the unit's power in that spacecraft mode is not known.
- **What to do.** Use a power mode listed under `modes` in the unit file, or add it.

### UNIT_NOT_MAPPED

**A unit has no power mode in a spacecraft mode** (error)

- **Rule.** Every unit must be assigned a power mode in every spacecraft mode.
- **Why it matters.** A unit left out would be counted as drawing nothing.
- **What to do.** Add `<unit>: <power mode name>` under `assignments` of the spacecraft mode.

### REF_UNKNOWN_PHASE

**A mission phase is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** A phase named in a file must be one of `mission_phases` in spacecraft.yaml.
- **Why it matters.** Limits and masses are tied to phases.
- **What to do.** Use a name listed under `mission_phases`, or add the phase.

### PHASE_MASS_MISSING

**An expendable has no mass for a phase** (error)

- **Rule.** An expendable needs a mass for every mission phase.
- **Why it matters.** A missing phase would count the item as massless in that phase.
- **What to do.** Add an entry named like the phase, with its mass in kg (0.0 if it is not aboard).

### REF_UNKNOWN_MODE

**A spacecraft mode is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** A spacecraft mode named in a file (a thermal case, a link, a scenario rule) must be a file in modes/.
- **Why it matters.** The mode decides which power modes, and so which dissipation, apply.
- **What to do.** Use the id of a mode in modes/.

## Mass budget

### MASS_FRAME_UNDEFINED

**Positions are given but the body frame is not described** (warning)

- **Rule.** If any item has a position, `body_frame` in spacecraft.yaml should describe the axes and the origin.
- **Why it matters.** A centre of gravity is only meaningful in a stated frame.
- **What to do.** Describe the axes and origin in `body_frame`.

### MASS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

**A mass limit is exceeded** (error)

- **Rule.** The system-margined total mass of a phase must not exceed any mass limit that applies to the phase.
- **Why it matters.** The limit is a requirement on the design (a launcher capacity, a budget allocation).
- **What to do.** Reduce mass, review the margins, or change the limit (and cite its source).

### MASS_PROPS_MISSING

**An item has no position** (warning)

- **Rule.** An item with a mass should have `mass_properties.position_m`.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the item is left out of the centre of gravity and the inertia (it is never counted at the origin), so those results cover only part of the mass.
- **What to do.** Add `mass_properties` with `position_m: [x, y, z]` in the body frame.

### MASS_INERTIA_POINT_MASS

**An item is treated as a point mass** (info)

- **Rule.** An item with a position but no own inertia contributes only the parallel-axis term.
- **Why it matters.** The inertia of the spacecraft is a little low by the item's own inertia.
- **What to do.** Add `mass_properties.inertia` if the item's own inertia matters.

### MASS_INERTIA_NOT_SCALED

**An expendable's inertia does not follow its mass** (warning)

- **Rule.** An expendable with an own inertia and more than one mass uses the same inertia in every phase (DEVIATIONS DV-M4).
- **Why it matters.** The inertia is wrong in the phases where the mass differs.
- **What to do.** Remove the own inertia (point mass) or accept the error; per-phase inertia is not modelled.

## Thermal budget

### REF_UNKNOWN_CASE

**A thermal case is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** A surface exposure must name a case defined in the thermal environment.
- **Why it matters.** An exposure for an unknown case would never be used.
- **What to do.** Use a case listed under `cases` in config/thermal_environment.yaml.

### THERMAL_NODE_UNKNOWN

**A thermal node is not defined** (error)

- **Rule.** The node named by a unit or a surface must be a node of the thermal model.
- **Why it matters.** Heat put into an undefined node would be lost from the balance.
- **What to do.** Use a node listed under `nodes` in config/thermal_model.yaml.

### THERMAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

**A unit is outside its temperature limits** (error)

- **Rule.** In every thermal case the temperature of a unit's node must lie between the lower and the upper limit of the limit set the case uses (operating or survival).
- **Why it matters.** The limits come from the unit's data sheet; outside them it is not qualified.
- **What to do.** Change the design (conduction, radiator area, dissipation) or the limit, citing its source.

### THERMAL_MARGIN_INSUFFICIENT

**A unit is closer to its limit than the required margin** (error)

- **Rule.** The headroom to each temperature limit must be at least `temperature_margin_k`.
- **Why it matters.** The margin covers the uncertainty of the model.
- **What to do.** Change the design, or review the required margin in config/thermal_environment.yaml.

### THERMAL_NO_LIMITS

**A unit has no temperature limits** (warning)

- **Rule.** A unit should have limits for the set a case checks.
- **Why it matters.** It is not checked, which is not a pass.
- **What to do.** Add `temperature_limits` from the unit's data sheet.

### THERMAL_SOLVE_FAILED

**The node temperatures cannot be solved** (error)

- **Rule.** Every group of connected nodes needs a path to space (a surface that radiates), otherwise there is no equilibrium.
- **Why it matters.** Without an equilibrium no temperature is computed.
- **What to do.** Give every group of connected nodes a surface that radiates to space.

## Link budget

### REF_UNKNOWN_ATTENUATION

**A link names an attenuation that has no table entry** (error)

- **Rule.** Each attenuation a link names must have an entry in config/attenuation_table.yaml.
- **Why it matters.** The tool has no propagation model of its own; the loss comes only from the table.
- **What to do.** Use a name listed under `entries`, or add the entry with its source.

### REF_UNKNOWN_MODULATION

**The Eb/N0 table has no entry for the modulation and coding** (error)

- **Rule.** A link's modulation and coding must be a pair in config/ebn0_table.yaml.
- **Why it matters.** The required Eb/N0 decides whether the link closes.
- **What to do.** Add the entry with its source (Edit, Add Eb/N0 entry in the window), or correct the names.

### REF_UNKNOWN_STATION

**The peer of a link is not a ground station** (error)

- **Rule.** A link's peer must be a file in ground_stations/.
- **Why it matters.** The peer decides where the passes of the link are computed.
- **What to do.** Use the id of a ground station.

### LINK_ANTENNA_PATTERN_GROUND

**A ground antenna has a pattern** (error)

- **Rule.** A ground antenna has a constant gain; patterns are for the spacecraft end.
- **Why it matters.** The tool assumes the ground antenna tracks the spacecraft.
- **What to do.** Use `gain_dbi` for the ground antenna.

### LINK_PATTERN_FILE_MISSING

**An antenna pattern file is missing** (error)

- **Rule.** A `pattern_file` must exist and lie inside the project folder.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the antenna gain is not known.
- **What to do.** Give a path relative to the project folder, to an existing CSV file.

### LINK_NOT_CLOSED

**A link closes at none of its data rates** (error)

- **Rule.** At least one listed data rate must give a margin of at least the required margin.
- **Why it matters.** A link that never closes cannot carry data.
- **What to do.** Lower the data rates, raise the transmit power or antenna gain, or review the losses and the required margin.

### LINK_INPUT_INVALID

**A link input cannot be used** (error)

- **Rule.** An antenna pattern file must lie inside the project folder and be a CSV table of increasing angles (`angle_deg`, `gain_dbi`).
- **Why it matters.** A pattern that cannot be read leaves the antenna gain unknown.
- **What to do.** Use a relative path and a comma-separated UTF-8 file with the two columns.

### LINK_ATTENUATION_FREQUENCY

**An attenuation entry is for another frequency** (warning)

- **Rule.** An attenuation entry used by a link should be for the link's frequency (within 1 %).
- **Why it matters.** A loss at the wrong frequency may be far from the loss at the link frequency.
- **What to do.** Use an entry for the link frequency.

### LINK_ATTENUATION_DUPLICATE

**Two attenuation entries for one elevation** (warning)

- **Rule.** A named attenuation should have one entry per elevation.
- **Why it matters.** The larger loss is used, which may not be the one intended.
- **What to do.** Keep one entry per elevation.

### LINK_NO_STATIC_POINTS

**A link has no static points** (info)

- **Rule.** A link with no static points has no static table.
- **Why it matters.** Nothing is wrong; only the pass series (with a scenario) is available.
- **What to do.** Add elevation and range pairs under `static_points`.

### LINK_SITE_NOT_IN_SCENARIO

**The peer of a link is not a site of the scenario** (warning)

- **Rule.** The ground station a link names must be listed in the scenario's `sites`.
- **Why it matters.** Without it there is no pass series for the link.
- **What to do.** Add the ground station to `sites` of the scenario.

### LINK_NEVER_ACTIVE

**A link is never active in the scenario** (info)

- **Rule.** A link is active when a pass of its station falls in an active mode below the tracking limit.
- **Why it matters.** With no active time its data volume is zero.
- **What to do.** Check the scenario's sites and rules, `active_modes` and `max_elevation_deg` of the link.

### LINK_PER_DAY_NOT_GIVEN

**No data volume per day for a short scenario** (info)

- **Rule.** A per-day figure needs a scenario of at least one day.
- **Why it matters.** Scaling a short scenario to a day would repeat its passes.
- **What to do.** Use a scenario of at least one day.

## Scenarios and environment

### REF_UNKNOWN_ORBIT

**A scenario names an orbit that does not exist** (error)

- **Rule.** The orbit of a scenario must be a file in orbits/.
- **Why it matters.** The orbit decides every geometry in the scenario.
- **What to do.** Use the id of an orbit in orbits/.

### REF_UNKNOWN_SITE

**A site is not defined or not listed** (error)

- **Rule.** A site named by a scenario or one of its rules must exist, and a rule's site must be listed in the scenario's `sites`.
- **Why it matters.** A pass cannot be computed for a site the scenario does not have.
- **What to do.** Use the id of a ground station or target, and list it under `sites`.

### SCENARIO_UNKNOWN

**The scenario does not exist** (error)

- **Rule.** The scenario asked for must be a file in scenarios/.
- **Why it matters.** Nothing can be run without a scenario.
- **What to do.** Use one of the scenarios the message lists.

### SCENARIO_TOO_LARGE

**The scenario is too large** (error)

- **Rule.** The number of samples (duration over step) must fit the memory that is available.
- **Why it matters.** A run that exhausts memory would fail without a result.
- **What to do.** Increase `step_s` or shorten `duration_s`.

### SCENARIO_OPTION_IGNORED

**A scenario option has no effect** (warning)

- **Rule.** An option that belongs to another environment source is not used.
- **Why it matters.** You may believe a setting is in force that is not.
- **What to do.** Remove the option, or change `environment_source`.

### SCENARIO_PHASE_NO_DOD

**The battery has no depth-of-discharge limit for this phase** (warning)

- **Rule.** The scenario's mission phase must have an entry in `battery.max_dod_ratio`.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the depth-of-discharge check is not evaluated, which is not a pass.
- **What to do.** Add the phase under `battery.max_dod_ratio` in config/power_system.yaml.

### IMPORT_DIR_MISSING

**The import folder is missing** (error)

- **Rule.** The SpaceMissionStudio import folder must be an existing folder inside the project folder.
- **Why it matters.** Without it the imported positions cannot be read.
- **What to do.** Give a path relative to the project folder to an existing folder.

### ENV_INPUT_INVALID

**The imported environment files cannot be read** (error)

- **Rule.** The imported files must have the layout of docs/ENVIRONMENT_FORMAT.md.
- **Why it matters.** Positions that cannot be read would leave the scenario without an environment.
- **What to do.** Check the files against the format description.

### ENV_PROPAGATION_FAILED

**The orbit cannot be computed** (error)

- **Rule.** The orbit must be computable for the scenario dates (years 1950 to 2100; no decay).
- **Why it matters.** Without positions there are no passes, eclipses or Sun directions.
- **What to do.** Check the scenario start and duration, and the orbit; very low or very eccentric orbits decay.

### ORBIT_INVALID

**The orbit definition is not valid** (error)

- **Rule.** The elements or the TLE must describe an orbit above the Earth's surface.
- **Why it matters.** An orbit that touches the Earth cannot be propagated.
- **What to do.** Check the elements (a perigee below the surface is not valid) or the TLE lines.

### ORBIT_EPOCH_FAR

**The TLE is far from the scenario** (warning)

- **Rule.** A TLE should be within 30 days of the scenario start.
- **Why it matters.** An old TLE drifts: the passes and eclipses may be wrong in time.
- **What to do.** Use a TLE from near the scenario dates, or an orbit given by elements.

## Power timeline

### BATTERY_DOD_EXCEEDED

**The battery discharges deeper than allowed** (error)

- **Rule.** The depth of discharge must not exceed `battery.max_dod_ratio` of the mission phase.
- **Why it matters.** Deep cycling shortens the battery life; the limit is the requirement on the design.
- **What to do.** Reduce the demand, add capacity or generation, or review the limit (cite its source).

### BATTERY_DEPLETED

**The battery is empty and the demand is not supplied** (error)

- **Rule.** The demand not supplied by the array or the battery must stay at zero.
- **Why it matters.** In flight the loads would drop out.
- **What to do.** Reduce the demand, add generation or battery capacity, or change the scenario.

### ORBIT_BALANCE_NEGATIVE

**An orbit generates less energy than it uses** (error)

- **Rule.** Over each orbit the energy generated must be at least the energy demanded.
- **Why it matters.** The battery would be drained orbit after orbit.
- **What to do.** Increase the array or reduce the demand; the table of orbit balances shows each orbit.

### PEAK_POWER_EXCEEDED

**The peak demand exceeds the power limit** (error)

- **Rule.** The peak power demand at the source must not exceed `limits.peak_power_w`.
- **Why it matters.** The limit is what the power system can deliver at once.
- **What to do.** Reduce the peak demand, or review the limit (cite its source).

### ORBIT_BALANCE_NOT_EVALUATED

**The orbit energy balance was not evaluated** (warning)

- **Rule.** The energy balance needs a step of at most a quarter of the orbit period to find the orbits.
- **Why it matters.** Its absence is not a pass; the other checks do not depend on it.
- **What to do.** Use a shorter step.

### POWER_REFINEMENT_INCOMPLETE

**The battery full and empty instants were still moving** (warning)

- **Rule.** The instants at which the battery becomes full or empty are refined in rounds; they should settle within four.
- **Why it matters.** The energy results are accurate to the last edges found, not exact.
- **What to do.** Use a shorter step; report the project if it persists.

## Unit tables (import)

### IMPORT_FILE_UNREADABLE

**The unit table cannot be read** (error)

- **Rule.** A unit table is a .csv file (UTF-8) or an .xlsx workbook with at least a header row.
- **Why it matters.** Nothing can be imported from a file that cannot be read.
- **What to do.** Start from the template written by `budget units-export`.

### IMPORT_FILE_TOO_LARGE

**The unit table is too large** (error)

- **Rule.** A unit table is a few kilobytes.
- **Why it matters.** A very large file is probably not a unit table.
- **What to do.** Check that this is the right file.

### IMPORT_COLUMN_MISSING

**A column of the template is missing** (error)

- **Rule.** The table must have the columns of the template.
- **Why it matters.** Without a required column the rows cannot be understood.
- **What to do.** Start from the template written by `budget units-export`.

### IMPORT_COLUMN_IGNORED

**A column is not used** (warning)

- **Rule.** Columns that are not in the template are ignored.
- **Why it matters.** Values in them have no effect.
- **What to do.** Remove the column or move the value to a column of the template.

### IMPORT_UNKNOWN_UNIT

**A row names a unit the project does not have** (error)

- **Rule.** An import changes existing units only.
- **Why it matters.** A new unit needs more than the power table gives.
- **What to do.** Use the ids of the exported template.

### IMPORT_FIELD_MISSING

**A row has no power mode name** (error)

- **Rule.** Each row names the power mode it describes.
- **Why it matters.** A row without it cannot be matched.
- **What to do.** Give the name of the power mode, as in the exported template.

### IMPORT_DUPLICATE_ROW

**A unit and power mode appear twice** (error)

- **Rule.** A unit and power mode pair may appear once.
- **Why it matters.** Two rows would disagree about the same numbers.
- **What to do.** Keep one row per power mode.

### IMPORT_VALUE_INVALID

**A value in the table cannot be used** (error)

- **Rule.** Each cell must be a number, or a number with a unit of the right dimension.
- **Why it matters.** The value would otherwise change the unit's power silently.
- **What to do.** Write a number or a value with a matching unit such as `2.5 W`; the message says what the field requires.

## Other

### INTERNAL_ERROR

**The tool failed unexpectedly** (error)

- **Rule.** The tool did not expect this failure; it reports only its kind, never project content.
- **Why it matters.** Whatever was being computed has no result.
- **What to do.** Run `budget validate` on the folder to see the details, then report it.
